reasons.claim: At a 10% required return Berkshire's intrinsic value of 351 billion is far below the market cap, making it extremely overvalued for that return.
reasons.quote: then I get with the p ratio of 15 in 2032 I get to an intrinsic value of 351 billion dollars you compare that to the market capitalization and you can see how four a ten percent return Berkshire is extremely overvalued

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: discount rate, terminal p/e

reasons.claim: The expected return implied by the current price is well below his required 10%, so the ratio of value to price is below one and he would not invest.
reasons.quote: I expect to return much below 10 that's the ratio is below one which means I would not invest in Berkshire now

reasons.claim: 123 billion in cash makes Berkshire a financial fortress that can't go bust, which is the foundation for compounding.
reasons.quote: it has 123 billion in cash on its balance sheet and that is a staggering number and that shows the quality of it and it can't go bust

data_check.gap_note: he says 1.23e+11, as-of 8.8706e+10 (FY2021); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: Reported earnings understate true earnings because retained earnings from stakes like Apple are not fully accounted for, adding hidden value.
reasons.quote: there is 4.6 billion that is not accounted into Berkshires earnings

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: Apple stake earnings not accounted, Berkshire's Apple ownership

reasons.claim: The best time to buy Berkshire is when the market hates Buffett and the P/E falls near 10, as in past crashes, not now when it's loved and expensive at a P/E near 20.
reasons.quote: when people love Berkshire when they look for safety Warren Buffett Etc it is expensive

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: historical p/e range, current p/e

external_facts_used: Berkshire's ownership stake of 5.6% in Apple and Apple's ~100 billion in profit
Berkshire's 15 owner's manual principles from January 1999
1998–2002 historical episode where Berkshire fell out of favor then outperformed as the S&P 500 crashed
Warren Buffett's original purchase price of Berkshire stock at $14.86

critic.notes: ok — he explicitly says he would not invest now, expected return well below 10%, extremely overvalued at 10% required return; only buys when hated at P/E ~10. Reason 5 quote swaps 'where' for 'when'.
